mainTopic: Remarrying a divorced wife after a vow or after divorcing her as an אילונית, and the rule against redeeming a man who sells himself to גוים.
overview: The amud finishes explaining the משנה about a husband who vowed 'קונם if I do not divorce you.' רב הונא explains that he forbade all food in the world on himself unless he divorced her. The גמרא explains why the משנה needs to say he may remarry her, using רבי נתן's harsh view of vows. רב ששת and רבינא then argue over where the phrase מפני תיקון העולם belongs. Next comes a new משנה: may a man remarry a wife he divorced as an אילונית? רבי יהודה says no and the חכמים say yes. The גמרא points out that this seems to reverse their opinions from the earlier vow משנה. שמואל swaps the names, אביי explains רבי יהודה's vow ruling with special reasons, and רבא adds that the חכמים here are רבי מאיר, who needs a תנאי כפול. A third משנה rules that a man who sells himself to גוים is not redeemed. רב אסי limits this to someone who sold himself three times, and stories about רב הונא and רבי אמי test the rule, with the second story continuing on the next amud.

steps.title: What does 'קונם' mean in this case?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what the husband's word 'קונם' means in the story about the man in צידן.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is meant by 'קונם'?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks a clarifying question about the husband's vow in the משנה. This sets up רב הונא's answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Normally 'קונם' is a word used to make something forbidden like a קרבן. Here the husband said 'קונם if I do not divorce you,' but the sentence does not say what becomes forbidden. The גמרא wants to know the exact wording of the vow.

keyTerms.meaning: A vow word that makes something forbidden, like a קרבן
What is / what does it mean

phrases.english: What is 'konam'?
phrases.notes: This refers to the man in the משנה who told his wife 'קונם if I do not divorce you.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens the discussion of the משנה's story about the vow in צידן.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What exactly the husband forbade when he said 'קונם if I do not divorce you.'

steps.title: רב הונא: He forbade all the produce in the world on himself
steps.stepSummary: רב הונא explains that the husband said all the produce in the world should be forbidden to him unless he divorces her.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב הונא said: The case is when he says, 'All the produce in the world will be forbidden to me if I do not divorce her.'
steps.whatsHappening: רב הונא answers the question. The vow forbade all food in the world to the husband unless he divorces his wife.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Now we see why he felt forced to divorce her. If he did not, he could not eat anything at all. The vow pressured him into the divorce, and that is the background for the חכמים allowing him to remarry her.

keyTerms.meaning: Will become forbidden
Produce, fruits (here: all food)
Divorce her

phrases.english: Rav Huna said:
When he says: 'All the produce in the world will be forbidden to me
if I do not divorce her.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 1.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The vow forbade all produce in the world to the husband unless he divorced his wife.

steps.title: Why say he may remarry her? That is obvious
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes 'they permitted him to remarry her' and asks why the משנה needs to say something so obvious.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'And they permitted him to remarry her.' That is obvious!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes the next words of the משנה and challenges them as unnecessary. This sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The penalty in the משנה was for a woman's vow. Here the husband made the vow and the wife did nothing wrong. So why would anyone think he cannot take her back? The גמרא wants to know what new thing the משנה is teaching.

keyTerms.meaning: And they permitted
That he may take her back (remarry her)
It is obvious! (a challenge that the ruling teaches nothing new)

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix this up with the beginning of the משנה. There the wife made the vow, and he may not remarry her. Here the husband made the vow.

phrases.english: 'And they permitted him to remarry her':
It is obvious!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves on to the next words of the משנה, now that the case is clear.
steps.kashyaTarget: The משנה's statement that the חכמים permitted him to remarry her.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Nothing here seems to forbid remarrying her, so the ruling looks unnecessary.

steps.title: We might have penalized him because of רבי נתן's view of vows
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that we might have penalized him, because רבי נתן compares making a vow to building a forbidden altar. The משנה teaches that there is no such penalty.
steps.simpleTranslation: You might have said: Let us make a decree because of רבי נתן. As it was taught: רבי נתן says, one who vows is like someone who built a private altar, and one who keeps his vow is like someone who brought a קרבן on it. So the משנה teaches us that he may remarry her.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains why the משנה had to say he may remarry her. Without it, we might have punished him for vowing and then keeping his vow.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי נתן says vowing is like building a במה (a private altar, which was forbidden), and keeping the vow is like offering on it. This husband did both, so we might have thought the חכמים would penalize him by not letting him take her back. The משנה tells us they did not make such a decree.

keyTerms.meaning: You might have thought
Let us make a decree (a rabbinic penalty)
One who makes a vow
A private altar, forbidden while the בית המקדש stood
It teaches us (that the possible mistake is wrong)

steps.whyThisMatters: This shows how strongly some חכמים opposed making vows. Even so, the חכמים did not add a penalty here.

phrases.aramaic: מַהוּ דְּתֵימָא לִיגְזוֹר מִשּׁוּם דְּרַבִּי נָתָן –
phrases.english: You might have said: Let us make a decree because of Rabbi Natan –
as it was taught: Rabbi Natan says:
One who vows is as if he built a private altar,
and one who fulfills it is as if he offered a sacrifice on it;
it teaches us otherwise.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַהוּ דְּתֵימָא לִיגְזוֹר מִשּׁוּם דְּרַבִּי נָתָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the פשיטא challenge of step 3.
steps.terutzResolutionType: מהו דתימא: shows a real mistake the משנה needed to prevent
steps.terutzHavaAmina: We would have penalized the husband for vowing and keeping his vow, which רבי נתן treats as a serious sin, and forbidden him to remarry her.
steps.terutzMaskana: The חכמים made no such decree, so he may remarry her.

steps.title: How does letting him remarry her improve the world?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what תיקון העולם there is in letting the husband remarry his wife.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'For the betterment of the world': What betterment of the world is there?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes the משנה's reason, 'מפני תיקון העולם,' and asks how it fits this ruling. Two answers come next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: תיקון העולם usually explains why the חכמים added a restriction to prevent trouble. Allowing him to remarry her is a leniency, not a restriction. So the reason does not seem to match the ruling.

keyTerms.meaning: For the betterment of the world (a rabbinic reason to prevent problems)
There is

phrases.english: 'For the betterment of the world':
What betterment of the world is there?

steps.triggerLanguage: מִפְּנֵי תִּיקּוּן הָעוֹלָם: מַאי תִּיקּוּן הָעוֹלָם אִיכָּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves on to the last words of the משנה.
steps.kashyaTarget: The משנה's reason, 'מפני תיקון העולם,' attached to allowing him to remarry her.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The reason seems to fit a restriction, not the leniency of letting him take her back.

steps.title: רב ששת: The phrase goes back to the first part of the משנה
steps.stepSummary: רב ששת says 'מפני תיקון העולם' explains the first part of the משנה, where he may not remarry a wife he divorced over a bad name or a vow.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב ששת said: It refers to the first part of the משנה.
steps.whatsHappening: רב ששת answers that the phrase does not explain רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה's story at all. It explains the earlier ruling that forbids remarrying.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the first part of the משנה, a man who divorced his wife because of a bad name or a vow may not take her back. That restriction is the תיקון העולם. So the phrase fits a restriction after all, just not the one in this story.

keyTerms.meaning: On the first part (of the משנה)

phrases.english: Rav Sheshet said: It refers to the first clause.
phrases.notes: He means the start of the משנה: a man who divorces his wife over a bad name or a vow may not take her back.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: First answer to the challenge of step 5.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Moves the phrase to a different part of the משנה
steps.terutzHavaAmina: 'מפני תיקון העולם' explains the permission to remarry.
steps.terutzMaskana: It explains the earlier ban on remarrying a wife divorced over a bad name or a vow.

steps.title: רבינא: The phrase means 'there is no תיקון העולם concern here'
steps.stepSummary: רבינא keeps the phrase on the later part of the משנה and reads it as saying that this case has no תיקון העולם concern.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבינא said: Really, it refers to the later part, and this is what it means: In this case there is no concern of betterment of the world.
steps.whatsHappening: רבינא gives a different answer. He keeps the phrase on the story, but reads it as saying there is no תיקון העולם concern here.
steps.deeperAnalysis: According to רבינא, the תיקון העולם ban on remarrying applies only when the wife made the vow. When the husband made the vow, that reason does not apply, so he may take her back. He changes how we read the phrase instead of moving it to another part of the משנה.

keyTerms.meaning: Really, in fact (keeping the original reading)
On the later part (of the משנה)
And this is what it is teaching (a new way to read the words)

steps.whatToRemember: There are two ways to read 'מפני תיקון העולם.' רב ששת: it explains the earlier ban on remarrying. רבינא: it stays on the story and means 'there is no תיקון העולם concern here.' Both agree that a husband who divorced because of his own vow may remarry her.

phrases.english: Ravina said: Actually, it refers to the latter clause,
and this is what it teaches:
In this case there is no concern of betterment of the world.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A second answer to step 5, different from רב ששת's answer.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The phrase must either explain the permission or be moved to the first part of the משנה.
steps.terutzMaskana: The phrase stays on the later part and means that the תיקון העולם ban does not apply when the husband made the vow.

steps.title: Divorcing a wife believed to be an אילונית
steps.stepSummary: The משנה records a dispute. If a man divorces his wife because she is an אילונית, may he remarry her? רבי יהודה says no, and the חכמים say yes.
steps.simpleTranslation: משנה: A man who divorces his wife because she is an אילונית: רבי יהודה says he may not remarry her, and the חכמים say he may remarry her.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins with a dispute. The question is whether a man who divorced his wife because she could not have children may later remarry her.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is the same kind of question as the previous משנה about a bad name or a vow. Once he divorces her for this reason, can he take her back? רבי יהודה forbids it and the חכמים allow it.

keyTerms.meaning: A woman whose body never fully developed, so she cannot have children
He may not take her back (remarry her)
The Sages, the majority opinion

phrases.english: MISHNA:
One who divorces his wife because she is an ailonit,
phrases.notes: An אילונית is a woman who can't have children. The husband found this out after the wedding.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yehuda says: He may not remarry her.
And the Rabbis say: He may remarry her.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new משנה with a case parallel to the bad-name and vow cases discussed before.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי יהודה: he may not remarry a wife divorced as an אילונית. חכמים: he may remarry her.

steps.title: She has children with another man and claims her כתובה
steps.stepSummary: If the woman remarries, has children, and then claims her כתובה from the first husband, רבי יהודה says the husband may tell her that her silence is better than her speech.
steps.simpleTranslation: If she married another man and had children from him, and she then demands her כתובה, רבי יהודה said the first husband may say to her: your silence is better than your speech.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה continues with a follow-up case. The woman turns out not to be an אילונית, since she had children with someone else. Now she wants her כתובה from the first husband.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Her having children shows the first husband was wrong about her. She argues he owes her the כתובה. רבי יהודה lets the husband warn her that pushing this claim could backfire on her.

keyTerms.meaning: The marriage contract money a husband owes his wife at divorce
She demands, makes a claim
Your silence is better than your speech

phrases.english: If she married another man
and had children from him,
and she is demanding her marriage contract;
Rabbi Yehuda said: he may say to her:
Your silence is preferable to your speech.
phrases.notes: He's hinting that if she keeps pushing, he may claim the whole divorce was a mistake. That could hurt her and her children.

steps.triggerLanguage: נִישֵּׂאת לְאַחֵר וְהָיוּ לָהּ בָּנִים הֵימֶנּוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the same משנה with a follow-up case about the same woman.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי יהודה: when she claims her כתובה after having children with another man, the first husband may tell her that her silence is better than her speech.

steps.title: The opinions seem reversed from the earlier משנה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks whether רבי יהודה worries about future harm here and the חכמים do not. Elsewhere, we heard the opposite from them.
steps.simpleTranslation: גמרא: Does this mean that רבי יהודה worries about harm and the חכמים do not? But we have heard the opposite from them!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא raises a contradiction. In our משנה, רבי יהודה seems to be the one worried about harm. But we know the opposite from somewhere else, and the next step shows where.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Forbidding remarriage is a protection. If the husband knows he can never take her back, he will only divorce her if he is sure, and will not later claim the divorce was a mistake. So רבי יהודה, who forbids remarriage here, seems to worry about this harm, and the חכמים, who allow it, seem not to.

keyTerms.meaning: Is this to say? An opening that questions what follows from a statement
Is concerned, worries about
Harm, damage that could happen later
The reverse, the opposite

steps.confusionAlert: Don't mix up who is strict. Here, 'he may not remarry' is the opinion that worries about harm. רבי יהודה says that here, but the חכמים say it in the earlier משנה. That is exactly the contradiction.

phrases.english: GEMARA:
Is this to say that Rabbi Yehuda is concerned about potential harm,
phrases.notes: The 'harm' is the husband later claiming the divorce was a mistake, which could cast doubt on her status.

phrases.english: and the Rabbis are not concerned about potential harm?!
But didn't we hear the opposite from them!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Analyzes the dispute in step 8 and claims it conflicts with these same opinions elsewhere.
steps.kashyaTarget: The opinions of רבי יהודה and the חכמים in the אילונית dispute
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Each opinion here seems to take the opposite stance on worrying about harm from the one it takes in the earlier משנה, so the opinions look inconsistent.

steps.title: Proof from the bad-name and vow משנה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the earlier משנה. There, the חכמים forbid remarriage after any vow, while רבי יהודה allows it when the vow was not publicly known. So there, the חכמים worry about harm and רבי יהודה does not.
steps.simpleTranslation: As we learned: one who divorces his wife over a bad name may not remarry her, and one who divorces her over a vow may not remarry her. רבי יהודה says: for any vow the public knew about, he may not remarry her, and for one the public did not know about, he may. So the חכמים worry about harm, and רבי יהודה does not!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא backs up its question by quoting the earlier משנה, which shows the opinions the other way around.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the vow case, the חכמים forbid remarriage for every vow, which protects against the husband later regretting the divorce. רבי יהודה allows remarriage when the vow was private, so there he is the one less worried about that harm. This is the reverse of our משנה, and the contradiction now stands clearly.

keyTerms.meaning: As we learned in a משנה
A vow that many people knew about
Apparently, this shows that

steps.whatToRemember: The גמרא has set up a contradiction. In the אילונית case רבי יהודה is the one worried about harm, but in the vow case the חכמים are. The גמרא will need to explain why each opinion seems to switch.

phrases.english: As we learned:

phrases.aramaic: הַמּוֹצִיא אֶת אִשְׁתּוֹ מִשּׁוּם שֵׁם רַע – לֹא יַחְזִיר,
phrases.english: One who divorces his wife due to a bad reputation may not remarry her,
and if due to a vow, he may not remarry her.
Rabbi Yehuda says:

phrases.aramaic: כׇּל נֶדֶר שֶׁיָּדְעוּ בּוֹ רַבִּים – לֹא יַחְזִיר,
phrases.english: Any vow that the public was aware of, he may not remarry her,
but one that the public was not aware of, he may remarry her.
Apparently, the Rabbis are concerned about potential harm,
phrases.notes: Some versions don't have the words in square brackets; they're part of the corrected wording.

phrases.english: and Rabbi Yehuda is not concerned about potential harm!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supplies the source that shows the 'opposite' opinions claimed in step 10.
steps.raayaObject: The claim that the חכמים worry about harm and רבי יהודה does not
steps.raayaSupportSource: The earlier משנה on divorcing a wife over a bad name or a vow

steps.title: שמואל: Reverse the opinions
steps.stepSummary: שמואל answers the contradiction by switching the names in the אילונית משנה.
steps.simpleTranslation: שמואל said: Reverse the opinions. In the אילונית case, it is רבי יהודה who allows remarriage and does not worry, and the חכמים forbid it because they worry about future harm.
steps.whatsHappening: שמואל answers the contradiction by saying the names in the אילונית משנה should be swapped.
steps.deeperAnalysis: After the swap, the חכמים forbid remarrying the אילונית because they worry about future harm, and רבי יהודה allows it. Now each side is consistent with what it says in the vow משנה, where the חכמים worry and רבי יהודה does not.

keyTerms.meaning: Reverse! Switch which opinion belongs to which Tanna

phrases.english: Shmuel said: Reverse.
phrases.notes: He means: switch the names in the אילונית משנה, so רבי יהודה allows remarriage and the חכמים forbid it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the contradiction raised in steps 10-11.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reversing the attributions in one of the two contradicting sources
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The names in the אילונית משנה are correct as printed, which creates a contradiction with the vow משנה.
steps.terutzMaskana: Swap the names in the אילונית משנה, so the חכמים always worry about harm and רבי יהודה does not.

steps.title: The end of the משנה shows רבי יהודה worrying about harm
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא objects that the last part of the משנה clearly shows רבי יהודה worrying about harm, so a reversal of the first part alone does not work.
steps.simpleTranslation: But the end of the משנה teaches: if she married another man, had children from him, and then demands her כתובה, רבי יהודה said the husband can tell her, 'Your silence is better than your speech.' This implies that רבי יהודה does worry about harm!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges שמואל by quoting the end of the same משנה, where רבי יהודה clearly worries about a bad outcome.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the last part of the משנה, רבי יהודה lets the husband push back against her claim, because pressing it could cast doubt on her children's status. That is a concern about future harm. So even after שמואל's swap, רבי יהודה still looks like someone who worries about harm.

keyTerms.meaning: The last part of the משנה
By implication; we can learn from this
He is concerned about a future harm or bad outcome
Your silence is better than your speech

phrases.english: But from the fact that it teaches in the last clause:
She married another man
and she had children from him,
and she is demanding her כתובה;
phrases.notes: She is demanding it from the first husband, who divorced her.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yehuda said: he says to her:
"Your silence is better than your speech"
This implies that Rabbi Yehuda is concerned about harm!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks שמואל's reversal from step 12.
steps.kashyaTarget: שמואל's swap of the opinions in the אילונית משנה
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The end of the same משנה, which still bears רבי יהודה's name, shows him worrying about harm. So swapping only the first part leaves רבי יהודה inconsistent.

steps.title: Reverse the end of the משנה too
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that the end of the משנה should also be reversed and given to the חכמים.
steps.simpleTranslation: Here too, reverse the opinions, so the חכמים are the ones who say 'Your silence is better than your speech.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא defends שמואל by applying his reversal to the end of the משנה as well.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the end of the משנה is also swapped, the חכמים are the ones who worry about harm there. Now the whole picture is consistent: the חכמים worry about harm everywhere, and רבי יהודה does not.

keyTerms.meaning: This one too

phrases.english: This too, reverse.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 13 by extending שמואל's reversal.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Extending the reversal to the end of the משנה
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Only the first part of the משנה is reversed, so רבי יהודה still worries about harm at the end.
steps.terutzMaskana: The end is reversed too, so the חכמים are the ones who say 'Your silence is better than your speech.'
steps.whatToRemember: According to שמואל, the names in the whole אילונית משנה are swapped: the חכמים consistently worry about future harm, and רבי יהודה consistently does not.

steps.title: אביי: Don't reverse; רבי יהודה's vow ruling has special reasons
steps.stepSummary: אביי keeps the names as written. He explains that רבי יהודה's leniency in the vow case rests on reasons he shares with רבי מאיר and רבי אלעזר, not on a general lack of concern for harm.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said: Actually, do not reverse. In that vow case, רבי יהודה holds partly like רבי מאיר and partly like רבי אלעזר. For a vow that needs a חכם to release it, he holds like רבי אלעזר. For a vow that does not need a חכם, he holds like רבי מאיר.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי offers a different answer. He keeps the משנה as printed and explains why רבי יהודה's vow ruling does not prove he ignores future harm.
steps.deeperAnalysis: אביי accepts that רבי יהודה really does worry about harm, as the אילונית משנה shows. His lenient ruling in the vow case comes from specific reasons about vows that he takes from רבי מאיר and רבי אלעזר. Which reason applies depends on whether the vow needs a חכם. So for רבי יהודה, the vow case is a special exception, not a contradiction.

keyTerms.meaning: Actually, really; keeps the original reading
In that one (the earlier vow משנה)
He holds like (a certain Tanna's view)
A vow that requires a חכם to release it

steps.confusionAlert: אביי is not saying רבי יהודה ignores future harm. He is saying רבי יהודה does worry about it, and that the vow case is lenient only because of special reasons that apply to vows.

phrases.english: Abaye said: Actually, do not reverse,
and Rabbi Yehuda, in that one,
phrases.notes: "That one" is the earlier משנה about divorcing a wife because of a vow.

phrases.english: holds like Rabbi Meir
and holds like Rabbi Elazar:
in a case that requires, he holds like Rabbi Elazar,
phrases.notes: "Requires" means a vow that needs a חכם to release it.

phrases.aramaic: בְּשֶׁאֵינוֹ צָרִיךְ סָבַר לַהּ כְּרַבִּי מֵאִיר.
phrases.english: in a case that does not require, he holds like Rabbi Meir.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a different answer from שמואל's reversal in steps 12-14.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Distinguishing the cases: special reasons apply in the vow case
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבי יהודה's leniency in the vow case shows that he never worries about future harm.
steps.terutzMaskana: רבי יהודה does worry about harm. His vow ruling rests on reasons taken from רבי מאיר and רבי אלעזר, depending on whether the vow needs a חכם.

steps.title: רבא: What about the contradiction in the חכמים?
steps.stepSummary: רבא objects that אביי only solved רבי יהודה's contradiction and did not deal with the חכמים's contradiction. The next step gives רבא's own answer.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: Is רבי יהודה against רבי יהודה a difficulty, but the חכמים against the חכמים not a difficulty?!
steps.whatsHappening: רבא challenges אביי's answer, saying it leaves half the problem unsolved.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The original contradiction had two sides. רבי יהודה seemed inconsistent, and so did the חכמים, who worry about harm in the vow case but not in the אילונית case. אביי explained only רבי יהודה's side, so the חכמים still look inconsistent.

keyTerms.meaning: Against; one statement compared to another
A difficulty, a contradiction
The חכמים, the majority Sages

phrases.english: Rava said:
Is Rabbi Yehuda against Rabbi Yehuda difficult,
but the Rabbis against the Rabbis not difficult?!

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּרַבִּי יְהוּדָה אַדְּרַבִּי יְהוּדָה קַשְׁיָא, דְּרַבָּנַן אַדְּרַבָּנַן לָא קַשְׁיָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks אביי's answer in step 15 as incomplete.
steps.kashyaTarget: אביי's resolution that keeps the original attributions
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The contradiction applied to both sides. אביי resolved only רבי יהודה's inconsistency, so the חכמים still worry about harm in the vow case but not in the אילונית case.

steps.title: רבא's own answer: the Sages here are רבי מאיר, who needs a doubled condition
steps.stepSummary: רבא accepts אביי's answer for רבי יהודה. To solve the חכמים's side, he says the חכמים of the אילונית משנה are רבי מאיר, who requires a תנאי כפול, and here the husband did not double his condition.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, רבא said: רבי יהודה against רבי יהודה is not a problem, as we already answered. The חכמים against the חכמים is also not a problem. Who are the חכמים here? רבי מאיר, who says a condition must be doubled. And here we are dealing with a man who did not double his condition.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא now gives his own full answer. He fixes the part he said אביי left open, which was the contradiction in the חכמים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For רבי יהודה, רבא simply uses אביי's answer from Step 15. For the חכמים, he says the 'חכמים' who let the husband remarry the אילונית are רבי מאיר. רבי מאיר holds that a condition only counts if it is said both ways (a תנאי כפול). This husband only said 'I divorce you because you are an אילונית' and never said the other side, so his condition does not count. That is why the חכמים can let him take her back here, even though they worry in the vow case.

keyTerms.meaning: A doubled condition: stating both sides, 'if X, then this; and if not X, then not this'
As we answered (pointing back to an earlier answer)
And here, what case are we dealing with? (introduces a narrowing of the case)
Against, contradicting (as in 'this one against that one')

steps.whatToRemember: רבא's final answer: רבי יהודה is explained as אביי said. The חכמים of the אילונית case are רבי מאיר, and the husband's condition there was not doubled, so it does not count.
steps.confusionAlert: Do not think רבא is arguing with the vow-case reasoning. He agrees the חכמים worry in general. In the אילונית case the husband's condition simply has no legal force, because it was not doubled.
steps.whyThisMatters: This shows a common גמרא tool: an anonymous 'חכמים' can be identified with one specific תנא whose known rules then explain the ruling.

phrases.english: Rather, Rava said:

phrases.aramaic: דְּרַבִּי יְהוּדָה אַדְּרַבִּי יְהוּדָה לָא קַשְׁיָא –
phrases.english: Rabbi Yehuda against Rabbi Yehuda is not difficult
as we answered.
phrases.notes: He means אביי's answer from Step 15.

phrases.english: The Rabbis against the Rabbis is not difficult,
who are the Sages? Rabbi Meir,
who said: we require a doubled condition,
phrases.notes: A doubled condition spells out both sides: what happens if it's true and what happens if it's not.

phrases.english: and here, what are we dealing with?
where he did not double his condition.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רבא's own objection in Step 16 by adding an answer for the חכמים while keeping אביי's answer for רבי יהודה.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Identifying the anonymous חכמים with רבי מאיר and narrowing the case (the condition was not doubled)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The חכמים seem to worry about trouble later in the vow case but not in the אילונית case, which looks like a contradiction.
steps.terutzMaskana: The חכמים of the אילונית case are רבי מאיר. Since the husband did not double his condition, it has no force, so he may remarry her.

steps.title: New משנה: one who sells himself and his children to gentiles
steps.stepSummary: The משנה rules that a Jew who sells himself and his children to גוים is not redeemed, but his children are redeemed after his death.
steps.simpleTranslation: משנה: Someone who sells himself and his children to גוים is not redeemed. But the children are redeemed after their father dies.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins with a new case. A man who sold himself to גוים is not bought back, but his children are, once he has died.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The father brought this on himself, so the community does not redeem him. The children did nothing wrong, so they are redeemed. The children are only redeemed after the father's death, not while he is alive.

keyTerms.meaning: Our משנה
We redeem, we buy back a captive or slave
One who sells himself (as a slave)

phrases.english: Mishnah

phrases.aramaic: הַמּוֹכֵר אֶת עַצְמוֹ וְאֶת בָּנָיו לַגּוֹיִם –
phrases.english: One who sells himself and his children to gentiles
we do not redeem him,
but we redeem the children
after their father's death.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַתְנִי׳ הַמּוֹכֵר אֶת עַצְמוֹ וְאֶת בָּנָיו לַגּוֹיִם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic after the אילונית discussion ends.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A man who sells himself and his children to גוים is not redeemed. His children are redeemed after his death.

steps.title: רב אסי: only when he sold himself three times
steps.stepSummary: רב אסי limits the משנה. The father is not redeemed only if he sold himself a first, second and third time.
steps.simpleTranslation: גמרא: רב אסי said: This is only when he sold himself, did it again, and did it a third time.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens with רב אסי narrowing the משנה's rule. Not every man who sells himself loses the right to be redeemed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Read alone, the משנה sounds like a man is never redeemed after selling himself even once. רב אסי says the rule only applies to someone who sold himself three times. Only a repeat offender is denied redemption.

keyTerms.meaning: The Talmud's discussion of the משנה
And this is only when (a phrase that limits a rule)
And did it a second time and a third time

steps.whyThisMatters: This limit becomes the basis for testing the story that follows about the people of בי מיכסי.

phrases.english: Gemara
Rav Asi said:
And this is when he sold, and did it again, and did it a third time.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב אַסִּי וְהוּא שֶׁמָּכַר וְשָׁנָה וְשִׁילֵּשׁ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Narrows the משנה's rule in Step 18.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A man is denied redemption only if he sold himself three times.

steps.title: Story: the residents of בי מיכסי seized by gentile lenders
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא tells of people from בי מיכסי who borrowed from גוים, could not repay, and were seized. The case was brought to רב הונא.
steps.simpleTranslation: There were some people of בי מיכסי who borrowed money from גוים and could not pay it back. The lenders came and seized them. They came before רב הונא.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins a story to set up the next move. It describes the case first, before we hear רב הונא's response.
steps.deeperAnalysis: These people did not sell themselves outright. They borrowed money and were taken because they could not pay. The story asks whether the משנה's rule applies to them.

keyTerms.meaning: Those (introduces a story about certain people)
They borrowed
They seized, dragged off

phrases.english: Those residents of Bei Mikhsi,
who borrowed money from gentiles
and did not have enough to repay them.
They came and seized them,
phrases.notes: The gentile lenders are the ones who came and took the borrowers.

phrases.english: they came before Rav Huna.

steps.triggerLanguage: הָנְהוּ בְּנֵי בֵּי מִיכְסֵי דְּיָזְפִי זוּזֵי מִגּוֹיִם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a real case that tests the משנה and רב אסי's limit.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Sets up a case: borrowers from גוים were seized for unpaid debt and brought their case to רב הונא.

steps.title: רב הונא cites the משנה: he cannot help them
steps.stepSummary: רב הונא says he cannot help, and quotes the משנה that one who sells himself to גוים is not redeemed.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to them: What can I do for you? We learned in a משנה: Someone who sells himself and his children to גוים is not redeemed.
steps.whatsHappening: רב הונא answers the people. He uses our משנה as his proof that he cannot order that they be redeemed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב הונא treats borrowing and being seized for the debt like selling oneself. So the משנה's rule of 'we do not redeem him' applies. His answer sets up a question: does it fit רב אסי's limit of three sales?

keyTerms.meaning: What can I do for you?
As we learned in a משנה

steps.confusionAlert: רב הונא quotes only the first half of the משנה, the part about not redeeming the father. The part about redeeming the children after his death is not quoted here.

phrases.english: He said to them: What can I do for you,
as we learned:

phrases.aramaic: הַמּוֹכֵר אֶת עַצְמוֹ וְאֶת בָּנָיו לַגּוֹיִם –
phrases.english: One who sells himself and his children to gentiles
is not redeemed.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives רב הונא's response to the case set up in Step 20.
steps.raayaObject: רב הונא's refusal to have the seized borrowers redeemed
steps.raayaSupportSource: The משנה in Step 18: one who sells himself to גוים is not redeemed

steps.title: רבי אבא objects: the rule applies only after three sales
steps.stepSummary: רבי אבא challenges רב הונא. He was taught that the rule of not redeeming applies only to someone who sold himself three times, and that was not the case here.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אבא said to him: You, our teacher, taught me that this rule applies only when he sold himself, did it again a second time, and again a third time!
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אבא objects to רב הונא's refusal to help the captured men. He says the rule against redeeming does not fit this case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב הונא used the משנה's rule that one who sells himself to גוים is not redeemed. רבי אבא points to the known limit on that rule: it applies only after a first, second and third sale. These men were seized only once, so the rule should not apply to them.

keyTerms.meaning: You taught me
Our teacher, our master
Did it a second time and a third time

phrases.english: Rabbi Abba said to him:
phrases.notes: He is speaking to רב הונא, who just refused to help in step 21.

phrases.english: You, our master, taught me,
and that is only when he sold himself, and did it a second time, and a third time!

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַבִּי אַבָּא: לִימַּדְתַּנִי רַבֵּינוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רב הונא's use of the משנה in step 21
steps.kashyaTarget: רב הונא's refusal to redeem the men of בי מיכסי
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The rule of not redeeming applies only after three sales, and these men were not repeat sellers

steps.title: רב הונא answers: these men do this all the time
steps.stepSummary: רב הונא answers that these people habitually behave this way, so they count like someone who sold himself many times.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: These people are used to doing this regularly.
steps.whatsHappening: רב הונא defends his ruling. He explains that these men act this way all the time.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב הונא accepts the three-sale limit. He argues that these men's regular habit of borrowing and being seized puts them in the same group as a repeat seller. So the rule against redeeming does apply to them.

keyTerms.meaning: They are very used to it, it is their regular habit
That they do this

phrases.english: He said to him: These people are habitually used to it,
phrases.notes: רב הונא is now answering רבי אבא.

phrases.english: that they do this.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: הָנֵי מִרְגָּל רְגִילִי דְּעָבְדִי הָכִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רבי אבא's challenge from step 22
steps.terutzResolutionType: Redefining the case: habitual behavior counts like repeated selling
steps.terutzHavaAmina: These men were seized only once, so they should be redeemed
steps.terutzMaskana: Since they do this habitually, they are treated like someone who sold himself three times and are not redeemed
steps.whatToRemember: The rule of not redeeming someone who sold himself to גוים applies to repeat sellers. People who habitually get themselves seized are treated the same way.

steps.title: A man who sold himself to gladiators comes before רבי אמי
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא begins a new story about a man who sold himself to לודאי and came before רבי אמי to speak with him.
steps.simpleTranslation: There was a certain man who sold himself to gladiators. He came before רבי אמי and said to him:
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens a new story about a man who sold himself to people who use men as fighters. This line only sets up the story; what he says comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is another real case about someone who sold himself to non-Jews. Selling himself to לודאי was very dangerous, so this case is likely to test the rule about redeeming in a new way.

keyTerms.meaning: Sold himself
Gladiators, people who make men fight, often to the death
Before him

phrases.english: A certain man sold himself to gladiators.
He came before Rabbi Ami,
and said to him:
phrases.notes: The man is speaking to רבי אמי here. His words come in the next part of the גמרא.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new story about the משנה's rule after the בי מיכסי story ends
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Setup only: a man who sold himself to gladiators comes to רבי אמי
